reason: Frozen rubric A3 and SCORE_SPEC: self-play RL that updates Generator and Solver weights; the generated task pool is transient training data for weights, not a persisted prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/agent-code artifact reused by later tasks. paper.title: Tool-R0: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Tool-Learning from Zero Data
paper.central_claim: A Generator and a Solver, both initialized from the same base LLM and trained separately with GRPO under complementary rewards (difficulty-band curriculum reward for the Generator), co-evolve from zero data into a tool-calling agent that beats SFT on curated human datasets.

evidence.quote: framework for training general purpose tool-calling agents from scratch with self-play RL,
evidence.support_explanation: Self-play RL framework; the improved object is the Solver (and Generator) weights.

evidence.quote: Both Generator and Solver are optimized with GRPO
evidence.support_explanation: Both roles are updated by weight training with separate parameters.

evidence.quote: We then freeze the trained Generator and use it to construct a high-quality dataset via deduplication, cross-verification, and difficulty-based curriculum ordering
evidence.support_explanation: The generated task pool is an intermediate training dataset built each iteration; it is not a persistent harness component read by later tasks.

evidence.quote: is trained on this curated dataset
evidence.support_explanation: The pool is consumed by Solver training and then superseded by the next iteration pool.

evidence.quote: we run self-play for three iterations each with 50 steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Three iterations; 2,000 curated tasks per iteration per the same section.

evidence.quote: achieves 47.84% average accuracy with zero curated data, outperforming methods trained on 4k-210k human-annotated examples.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result vs SFT baselines on the same 1.5B backbone (author-reported; single run).

evidence.quote: we conduct an ablation in which the Generator is frozen after initialization and used only to produce tasks via prompting
evidence.support_explanation: Frozen-generator ablation (47.84 -> 41.65 per Table 3) supports weight-side curriculum learning, not a retained harness artifact.

evidence.quote: Parameter separation between Generator and Solver is essential for stable co-evolution in open-ended agentic tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Shared-weight variant drops to 30.42 (Table 3); both roles are weight-level.

evidence.quote: Models trained on adaptive self-generated curricula outperform those trained on human expert data
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim, scoped to five tool-calling benchmarks and a 1.5B model for the supervised comparison.

signatures.object: Generator and Solver weights (Qwen2.5 / Llama-3.2 base LLMs); intermediate artifact = per-iteration curated task set
signatures.information: Generator: task specification (domain, context, #tools, #calls); reward from format, validity (tool menu vs gold call), and frozen Solver success rate in a band; Solver: tool menu, question, accuracy reward against the generated gold call
signatures.operation: GRPO on Generator; freeze it, synthesize 10,000 candidates, dedup and self-consistency filter, sort easy to hard, keep 2,000; GRPO on Solver; repeat three iterations
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable as a retained-harness selection: filtering decides training data, not a persisted artifact
signatures.failure_boundary: saturation after about three iterations for small models

claims.text: Zero-data self-play yields tool-calling agents that surpass fully supervised baselines.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Not rated (out of scope). Author-reported: dual-role GRPO self-play from a base LLM raises average tool-calling accuracy to a level above SFT on curated datasets on five benchmarks.
